_comment: The embedder registry: everything that varies from one embedder to the next, in
one place, keyed by model identity.
TWO MODELS SHIP, as separate aimee-kb image variants, because the choice is not
reversible per install: DB2 records the vector-column width and refuses startup on
drift, so 384 and 768 are not interchangeable once anything is embedded.
aimee-kb / aimee-kb-llm              bekko-a25m  (384)
aimee-kb-nomic / aimee-kb-nomic-llm  nomic-v2    (768)
Only the embedder named by the AIMEE_EMBEDDER build-arg is baked into a given
image. Both stay registered here because this file is the catalog of per-model
facts, not a manifest of what one image contains.
They ship as two images rather than one carrying both because nomic costs ~1.8GB
and runs ~6x slower on CPU. bekko is the default; nomic wins retrieval quality
(0.6075 vs 0.5909 NDCG@10; see docs/validation/embedder-selection-frozen-ab-v1.md).
A deployment that wants something else again points EMBEDDER_URL at its own
endpoint - that route needs no image, and its width may be anything up to
EMBED_MAX_DIM (4000, the DB2 column ceiling).
WHY THE PER-MODEL FACTS BELOW MATTER. Two of them fail SILENTLY when wrong, and
both have already gone wrong:
- pooling once defaulted to `last`, which is wrong for nomic. Wrong
pooling yields vectors that are correctly shaped, correctly normalised and
simply wrong. Nothing errors; recall collapses.
- prefixes were absent entirely, so nomic served at 0.5823 NDCG@10 instead of
the 0.6075 it was selected on - below the runner-up it was chosen over.
bekko needs no prefixes, so for that model the prefix machinery has no work to do.
It stays because the failure it prevents is undetectable at runtime, and because an
operator overlay (EMBEDDERS_EXTRA) can declare a prefixed model.
EVERY FIELD IS REQUIRED, including empty prefixes. A model whose card defines no
prefixes declares that with empty strings - readers distinguish 'declared none'
from 'not registered', and refuse to serve the latter rather than guess.
Derive these from the model card, never by copying another entry. `prefixes` comes
from the card's usage section, `pooling` from its 1_Pooling/config.json, `dim` from
that file's word_embedding_dimension, and `context` from max_trained_positions (NOT
the tokenizer's model_max_length, which is often a smaller artifact).

notes: The shipped embedder. 0.5909 NDCG@10 on frozen-ab-v1 (10,000 cases / 26,473
documents), ~6x nomic's CPU throughput and half its vector storage. Its card defines
NO prefixes, so the empty pair above is a declaration, not a gap — and its benchmark
number carries into production unchanged.
384-dim, confirmed against the card's 1_Pooling/config.json and our own table in
docs/validation/embedder-selection-frozen-ab-v1.md. An earlier entry here said 768,
which was wrong and would have been refused at serve time by the declared-dim check.
arch is ModernBertModel, hidden 384, max_position_embeddings 8192, 256k vocab
(multilingual).
Loaded in-container by sentence-transformers from repo@revision, baked at build time.
The wide/quality option, baked into the aimee-kb-nomic* image variants. 0.6075
NDCG@10 on frozen-ab-v1 (10,000 cases / 26,473 documents) WITH these prefixes.
Serving it WITHOUT them measures 0.5823 - below the 0.5909 runner-up it was chosen
over. The prefixes are not decoration; they are the number.
pooling is mean, from the card's 1_Pooling/config.json. It defaulted to `last` once,
which is wrong here, and produced correctly-shaped,
correctly-normalised, wrong vectors. Nothing errored; recall collapsed.
context 2048 is max_trained_positions; the tokenizer's model_max_length of 512 is an
artifact, not a limit.
768-dim. This is a ONE-WAY DOOR per install: DB2 records the vector-column width and
refuses startup on drift, so an install embedded at 384 cannot move here without a
full reindex. That is why it is a separate image rather than a runtime switch.
Costs ~1.8GB of image over bekko and runs ~6x slower on CPU, which is why both
variants ship instead of one image carrying both.
